newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Oct inflation rise slowest in 3 years.
newsitem.headline: Thai Oct inflation rise slowest in 3 years.

text.p: Despite widespread flooding across rural Thailand, year-on-year inflation grew at its slowest rate in three years in October, the Commerce Ministry said on Friday.

The consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.3 percent year-on- year in October against 4.6 percent in September and 6.6 percent a year ago, much to the surprise of most analysts who had expected a higher rise.
Anucha Kulvisuth of First Asia Securities Plc said he had expected a 4.8 percent CPI rise in October.

"We thought it should be higher than September's 4.6 percent. Unfortunately the improving figure comes out at a time the market is shifting attention to other issues like the current account deficit and sluggish exports," he told Reuters.
The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday Thai exports rose only 2.4 percent during the first eight months of this year against about 25 percent in the same period a year ago.
Analysts said the 1996 current account deficit would likely exceed last year's level of 8.1 percent of gross domestic product.
Songglod Bhichaikul of United Finance and Securities Plc said the market also expected to see higher October inflation because of firmer oil prices and a 8.3 percent minimum wage hike last month.

Nuchjarin Kasemsukworarat of Dhana Siam Finance and Securities said October inflation slowed on an annual basis as it was based partly on surging food prices in the same month last year when Thailand was hit by more severe flooding.

Deputy commerce minister Sukon Kanchanalai said a seasonal decline in domestic meat demand last month, when many Thais celebrated an annual vegetarian festival, helped depress prices of pork, beef, poultry and seafoods.
She said, however, that the festival raised prices of flour and flour products by 4.7 percent in October from September.
The minister said pig and poultry breeders had also raised production on expectations that floods would push up meat prices in October.
Analysts said the October CPI did not fall sharply enough to help bring overall 1996 inflation down to a government target of 5.5 percent.
The moving average CPI rose 6.0 percent in the first 10 months and analysts expected it to average 5.8 percent for the whole 1996.
